speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for National Development whether HDB is prepared to review the monthly household-income ceiling for prospective buyers of BTO flats and Executive Condominiums respectively, given the high inflation rate.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: Factors that are considered include the household incomes of Singaporeans and prevailing housing market conditions, among others.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: We are also mindful that lower-income households could be crowded out by an adjustment to the income ceilings.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: There is no income restriction for the purchase of a resale HDB flat on the open market.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: HDB is committed to helping Singaporeans, particularly first-timers and lower- to middle-income families, to own a home.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for National Development)
text: The Government will continue to monitor housing market conditions closely to ensure that public housing remains affordable and accessible.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The real income of Singaporeans may not increase this year and next year because of high inflation.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: But their nominal income will likely increase if inflation stays high at 5% this year, and probably next year at 10%.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, does this not affect only the income ceilings of application of BTO flats but also affect Singaporeans' income criteria eligibility for Enhanced Housing Grant, which means that $1,500 now get $80,000 of EHG, a lot of them may exceed $1,500 because of the increase in nominal income but not the real nominal income?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: My second supplementary question is that in 2010, the income ceiling for HDB BTO flats and the EC, the differential is $2,000 – that is, the difference between $8,000 and $10,000.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: And the average price of, say, a 3-bedroom EC, as compared to a, HDB 4-room flat, is probably more than double.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, could the Second Minister consider these two considerations?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I also understand his concern, which is about affordability and accessibility for HDB housing for the majority of Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: What HDB and MND do is to look at it as a whole, not just one lever or one particular measure in isolation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Overall, what we are trying to do is to look at the demand as well as the supply which, of course, in the pandemic years, has been somewhat constrained.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, to ensure that public housing remains affordable and accessible, one of our current priorities is to rein in the strong upward momentum in HDB resale prices.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Thus, any review to raise the income ceiling would also have to be balanced against greater competition for the finite resources of the Government.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, in short, what we are really saying is this.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We know that Singaporeans are keen to buy their HDB flats.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: On MND and HDB side, we will do our utmost to ensure that they remain affordable and accessible.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Tweaking the income ceiling, in and of itself, may not necessarily be the best measure.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will look at it overall and see how we can maintain that accessibility and affordability.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I was also asking about the income criteria to qualify for the various levels of the Enhanced Housing Grant and other housing grants.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, with the increase of the nominal income, you put a lot of people at a disadvantage that they cannot qualify for the higher housing grant.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second supplementary question is about the differential in gap between the HDB BTO income ceiling as well as the EC income ceiling.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The gap of $2,000 is quite different between today, which is a 14% difference, as compared to 2010 when it was a 25% difference.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I hope the Second Minister can answer the two questions.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If the Member is saying whether we can increase the grants, that is something we can look at.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: But, overall, the key message to the Member and to Singaporeans is that we will do whatever is necessary to ensure that housing remains affordable and accessible.
